ROOT-CAUSE PASS ON THE SEAMS FRONTIER, 2026-08-30, run under the root-cause skill after the trajectory band read `seams 18% (13/72) ← frontier` and the subsystem roll-up read `0 uncovered`. NEITHER NUMBER WAS RIGHT.

═══ ① THE CAUSE — AN ID'S SPELLING TREATED AS ITS TYPE ═══

`DesignGraph::lift_to_level` (crates/reflow2-core/src/maturity.rs) walked up the CONTAINS spine and chose a parent with:

    .find(|p| p.starts_with("cmp:") || p.starts_with("sys:"))

A NAMING CONVENTION STANDING IN FOR THE `level` DECLARATION. Ten of this design's eighteen subsystems are named `sub:*` — sub:tool-surface, sub:finding, sub:telling, sub:evidence, sub:serving, sub:change-and-structure, sub:across-designs, sub:surface-shaping, sub:session-posture, sub:install. Any module contained by one of those returned None from the lift, and the pair was then dropped from BOTH the coupling set and the contract set, so the roll-up went QUIET rather than wrong out loud.

═══ ② WHAT IT COST, MEASURED AGAINST THE COMMITTED EXPORT ═══

The function was replicated over docs/design/reflow2.json and reproduced the served answer exactly (8 couplings / 8 declared / 8 covered / 83 dropped), which is the check that it is the same computation. With the prefix test replaced by a Component-type test:

                                  as served      corrected
    modules that fail to lift     58 of 86       3 of 86
    subsystem couplings compared  8              19
    covered                       8              13
    uncovered                     0              6
    pairs dropped                 83             7

The six genuinely undeclared subsystem boundaries, invisible until now:
    sub:change-and-structure <-> sub:finding
    sub:change-and-structure <-> sub:telling
    sub:evidence <-> sub:finding
    sub:evidence <-> sub:telling
    sub:evidence <-> sys:time-history
    sub:finding <-> sub:telling

The three real lift failures are cmp:degraded, cmp:nudge and cmp:sync — the same three named in fact:ten-components-report-a-zero-blast-radius-the-source-contradicts as carrying no coupling edges at all. A separate, already-recorded defect of absence, not this one.

⭐ SO BOTH PUBLISHED READINGS WERE WRONG IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Module level said 18% and was measuring 72 in-process Rust call pairs against a vocabulary that cannot cover them. Subsystem level said 100% and was a FALSE ZERO — the shape fact:ten-components-report-a-zero-blast-radius-the-source-contradicts already names as the worst answer a coupling model can give, because it is the most reassuring reply available and therefore the one least likely to be questioned. The honest reading is 13 of 19, and six boundaries owe a contract.

═══ ③ THE CLASS, AND IT WAS RECORDED ONE DAY EARLIER ═══

fact:which-properties-are-node-references-is-a-judgement-made-once-and-never-recorded-for-the-others (2026-08-29) found nine dangling references and named the mechanism: *THE ID WAS CONSTRUCTED BY CONVENTION RATHER THAN RESOLVED BY LOOKUP.* This is the same class read in the other direction — the id was INTERPRETED by convention rather than resolved by lookup. One writes an id by guessing its spelling; the other reads a node's type out of its spelling. Both skip asking the graph what the node actually is.

The fix that generalises is therefore not 'add sub: to the list'. It is that an id prefix is a naming convention and carries no meaning a computation may read; `level`, `node_type` and the schema are where that meaning is declared.

═══ ④ WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT ═══

tests/seam_coverage.rs had five tests, all passing before and after the repair. Every fixture named its containers `sys:a` and `sys:b` — THE SUITE SHARED THE CODE'S ASSUMPTION. A blind spot in the implementation and a blind spot in its fixture were the same blind spot, so coverage of the function was high and coverage of the question was zero.

Pinned 2026-08-30 by two tests written against the unfixed code and OBSERVED FAILING: `a_container_is_found_by_its_level_not_by_how_its_id_is_spelled` (left 0, right 1) and `a_dropped_pair_is_reported_as_a_pair_not_as_an_endpoint`.

═══ ⑤ A SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT FOUND IN THE SAME FUNCTION ═══

`SeamSets.unreachable` increments once per PAIR and accumulates across both sets, but the scope_note called them `endpoint(s)`. On this design that printed '83 endpoint(s) reached no container', which reads as a count of orphaned components — and sent this investigation's first hypothesis (an incomplete containment spine) down a path the data refuted: 83 of 86 modules DO have a direct subsystem parent. Reworded to name pairs.

═══ ⑥ THE REST OF THE CODEBASE WAS SWEPT — THREE MORE SITES, ALL BENIGN ═══

A repo-wide grep for `starts_with("<id-prefix>")` over crates/, excluding tests, found exactly three others: heal.rs:1665, report.rs:1840 and structure.rs:299. ALL THREE READ `decision:ack:`, WHICH REFLOW2 MINTS ITSELF (detect.rs:1437, heal.rs:185) and reads back. Write and read are the same code, so a design that spells its ids differently cannot break them — which is precisely the failure mode that bit seam_coverage, where the ids were authored by whoever built the design. A WEAKER INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS AND NOT A LIVE DEFECT: a hand-authored Decision carrying that id would still be misread as a review record. Left alone deliberately, and recorded here so it is a judgement rather than an oversight.

═══ ⑦ NOT ESTABLISHED ═══

· Whether `sub:` versus `sys:` is a distinction anyone MEANT. Both are level `subsystem`; the prefixes carry no declared meaning. If they are meant to, that is a decision nobody has recorded, and this repair is correct either way.
· The six uncovered boundaries are NAMED, NOT SPECIFIED. What each contract says is design work awaiting the owner.
· Only `starts_with` was swept. Other spellings of the same mistake — `contains("cmp:")`, a regex over an id, a split on ':' — were not searched for.
